previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with recurrent mid-epigastric abdominal pain, nausea, and uncontrolled type 1 diabetes due to intentional insulin omission. She reported feeling more energetic without insulin, but presented with diabetic ketoacidosis, which resolved with subcutaneous insulin therapy. Her pain was consistent with her chronic pancreatitis, and she was maintained on her outpatient Dilaudid regimen. She tolerated oral intake without nausea or vomiting and was discharged home in stable condition after agreeing to resume insulin use. Follow-up with her primary care provider was arranged.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
## Abdominal pain: Ms. ___ is frequently admitted for similar 
abdominal pain and seeking IV narcotics, which is thought to be 
due to pancreatitis. Her PMD has set firm limits so that her 
regimen should be oral Dilaudid 2mg Q3H PRN. Thus, this is what 
she was prescribed, in addition to anti-emetics for severe 
gastroparesis. Although she continued to complain of pain and 
nausea, she was able to tolerate fried foods brought to her by 
visitors and pizza while in the hospital. No changes were made 
to her home medications for symptom management.  On day of 
discharge she continued to tolerate po and was discharged with 
home pain regimen, with dilaudid 2mg tab disp 20.  She will f/u 
with her pcp on ___
.
## DM Type 1 with acute hyperglycemia: Her fingersticks 
fluctuated widely during her admission, with occasional 
hypoglycemia. Her home dose of Lantus is 70U at bedtime. While 
in the hospital, she was treated with glargine 50 units plus a 
tighter sliding scale than per her home regimen. She was 
increased to glargin 60U qhs and iss when discharged and will 
have f/u with ___ on ___
.
## Urinary retention: While in the hospital, she developed 
urinary retention, which was likely ___ narcotic use, lack of 
ambulation, and diphenhydramine. Had had to receive straight 
catheterization for consistent bladder scans > 500cc. U/A and 
UCx did not reveal evidence of a UTI. On day of discharge foley 
was removed and patient was able to void on her own.  
.
## Anxiety, borderline personality, domestic violence: She was 
continued on her home Valium. She also had a 24-hour 1:1 sitter 
given prior physical violence against hospital staff. She was 
followed closely by the Social Work service, who knows her very 
well. She was also evaluated by the Domestic Violence team after 
she expressed that her roommate has been punching her in the 
face. She states that she plans to file a restraining order 
against him upon discharge.
.
